title: Spectrum of an exact Frobenius sequence
statement:
For a short exact sequence $0\to V'\to V\to V''\to0$ of finite
Frobenius modules whose maps commute with Frobenius, the spectrum of
$(V,F)$ (the multiset of the images under $\iota$ of the
eigenvalues, [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]) is the multiset
union of the spectra of $V'$ and $V''$, counted with algebraic
multiplicity.

proof.text: Write $K=\Qlb$, let $i:V'\to V$ and $p:V\to V''$ be the exact-sequence maps, and denote their Frobenius operators by $F',F,F''$. These are finite-dimensional $K$-spaces with linear automorphisms and the fixed field isomorphism $\iota$ of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights]. Put $S=i(V')=\ker p$. Equivariance gives $F(i(v'))=i(F'v')$, so $F(S)=S$. Choose bases $(e_a)$ of $V'$ and $(\bar e_b)$ of $V''$ and choose lifts $e_b\in V$ with $p(e_b)=\bar e_b$. The vectors $(i(e_a),e_b)$ form a basis of $V$: applying $p$ to a relation first makes every coefficient of the $e_b$ zero, then injectivity of $i$ makes the others zero; given $v$, subtract the lifted expansion of $p(v)$, leaving an element of $\ker p=i(V')$, proving spanning. Thus $\dim V=\dim V'+\dim V''$. In this basis $F$ has block matrix $\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\0&C\end{pmatrix}$, where $A$ is the matrix of $F'$ and $C$ that of $F''$: the first assertion follows from $Fi=iF'$ and the quotient coordinates follow from $pF=F''p$. No $F$-stable complement has been assumed.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: choose a basis of the subspace and lifts from the quotient

proof.text: Apply [p-linear-filtration] to the invariant filtration $0\subseteq S\subseteq V$. The maps $V'\to S$, $v'\mapsto i(v')$, and $V/S\to V''$, $[v]\mapsto p(v)$, are equivariant isomorphisms: bijectivity is respectively injectivity of $i$ and exactness plus surjectivity of $p$, and equivariance was checked in step 1. In the bases from step 1 their Frobenius matrices are literally $A$ and $C$. The cited determinant formula therefore gives $D_V(t)=D_{V'}(t)D_{V''}(t)$, where $D_W(t)=\det(1-tF_W\mid W)$. Set $\chi_W(T)=\det(T-F_W\mid W)$. In the Laurent polynomial ring $K[T,T^{-1}]$ one has $\chi_W(T)=T^{\dim W}D_W(T^{-1})$ by factoring $T$ out of every row of the defining determinant. Substitute $t=T^{-1}$ into the determinant product and use the dimension equality from step 1 to get $\chi_V(T)=\chi_{V'}(T)\chi_{V''}(T)$. All expressions in this last equality are polynomials; the inclusion of $K[T]$ into its Laurent polynomial ring is injective, since multiplying a polynomial by a power of $T$ shifts its coefficients. Hence the equality holds already in $K[T]$.

source.place: Proof, characteristic-polynomial identity; p-linear-filtration supplies the determinant product

proof.text:
For each $\alpha\in K$, let $r,s$ be its algebraic multiplicities as a root of the monic characteristic polynomials $\chi_{V'},\chi_{V''}$. Write $\chi_{V'}=(T-\alpha)^r u$ and $\chi_{V''}=(T-\alpha)^s v$ with $u(\alpha)
e0$ and $v(\alpha)
e0$. Step 2 gives $\chi_V=(T-\alpha)^{r+s}uv$, and $(uv)(\alpha)
e0$ because $K$ is a field. Thus the multiplicity on $V$ is exactly $r+s$. These characteristic polynomials are nonzero (their leading coefficient is $1$), so all multiplicities are finite. By the meaning of algebraic multiplicity, this proves equality of the eigenvalue multisets over $K$. The spectrum in the item is obtained by applying $\iota$ to each member of this multiset. Mapping a concatenation of finite lists maps each list separately, and passing to multisets therefore preserves multiset union. Applying this to the equality just proved gives the claimed complex spectra with multiplicities. The zero space has characteristic polynomial $1$ and empty multiset, so the same argument includes zero outer terms and the zero sequence; no semisimplicity is used.
